plain_english: It is said that the secret of the Trika scripture is the differentiation of the tattvas.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate trikaśāstrekarahasyaṃ tattvabhedanam

plain_english: The further difference among those tattvas, following in their own classes, is also declared in the scripture called Sri Trika.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāmamīṣāṃ tattvānāṃ svavargeṣvanugāminām bhedāntaramapi proktaṃ śāstre@tra śrītrikābhidhe

plain_english: By the difference of shaktiman and shakti, the range from earth to the root last is divided into fifteen by its own nature along with anara.
sanskrit_cite: śaktimacchaktibhedena dharādyaṃ mūlapaścimam bhidyate pañcadaśadhā svarūpeṇa sahānarāt

plain_english: Up to kala, with two differences omitted, pralayakala is rudra-like; similarly maya is ninefold, and jnakala is sevenfold again.
sanskrit_cite: kalāntaṃ bhedayugghīnaṃ rudravatpralayākalaḥ tadvanmāyā ca navadhā jñākalāḥ saptadhā punaḥ

plain_english: Mantras are those lords in fivefold, mantra-lords are threefold, but Shiva is not divided, being one light-dense consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: mantrāstadīśāḥ pāñcadhye mantreśapatayastridhā śivo na bhidyate svaikaprakāśaghanacinmayaḥ

plain_english: Shiva, mantra, mahesha, isha, mantra, akala, yuk, and kali are named; there are seven shaktimans and likewise fourteen shaktis.
sanskrit_cite: śivo mantramaheśeśamantrā akalayukkalī śaktimantaḥ sapta tathā śaktayastaccaturdaśa

plain_english: Its own nature is the fifteenth; that ground is fifteenth-natured, for the three powers of the Lord were described before.
sanskrit_cite: svaṃ svarūpaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tadbhūḥ pañcadaśātmikā tathāhi tisro devasya śaktayo varṇitāḥ purā

plain_english: Those very powers are established in the threefold form of knower, knowing, and known; the supreme part is knower-form here, and the instrument part is intermediate.
sanskrit_cite: tā eva mātṛmāmeyatrairūpyeṇa vyavasthitāḥ parāṃśo mātṛrūpo@tra pramāṇāṃśaḥ parāparaḥ

plain_english: The known is supreme; the power-holder part and power are its own nature; thus there the nature of the ground is that which stands separately as inert.
sanskrit_cite: meyo@paraḥ śaktimāṃśca śaktiḥ svaṃ rūpamityadaḥ tatra svarūpaṃ bhūmeryatpṛthagjaḍamavasthitam

plain_english: By conditions beginning with knower and knowing, not produced by stain; but by knowers from sakala to Shiva, its knowability is that which...
sanskrit_cite: mātṛmānādyupadhibhirasaṃjātoparāgakam sakalādiśivāntaistu mātṛbhirvedyatāsya yā

plain_english: By power-holders with unmanifest powers, seven divisions of those; from sakala to Shiva, in powers with raised self.
sanskrit_cite: śaktimadbhiranudbhūtaśaktibhiḥ sapta tadbhidaḥ sakalādiśivāntānāṃ śaktiṣūdrecitātmasu

plain_english: Knowability-born seven divisions; thus fourteen; of sakala, the instrument part which is vidya-kala-natured.
sanskrit_cite: vedyatājanitāḥ sapta bhedā iti caturdaśa sakalasya pramāṇāṃśo yo@sau vidyākalātmakaḥ

plain_english: That generic-natured portion is counted in power, not as distinct from it; layakala's measure-portion is that same generic, most clear.
sanskrit_cite: sāmānyātmā sa śaktitve gaṇito natu tadbhidaḥ layākalasya mānāṃśaḥ sa eva paramasphuṭaḥ

plain_english: But jnanakala's measure is the melting vidyakala-covering, joined with the impression of destroyed impure-knowledge activity.
sanskrit_cite: jñānākalasya mānaṃ tu galadvidyākalāvṛti aśuddhavidyākalanādhvaṃsasaṃskārasaṃgatā

plain_english: Yearning to awake, pure knowledge becomes the saviors' instrument; awakened, pure knowledge is joined with its own refinement.
sanskrit_cite: prabubhutsuḥ śuddhavidyā santrāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet prabuddhā śuddhavidyā tu tatsaṃskāreṇa saṃgatā

plain_english: The mantra-lords' measure is devoid of that impression; the mantra-great-lords' measure is called power as instrument.
sanskrit_cite: mānaṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ syāttatsaṃskāravivarjitā mānaṃ mantramaheśānāṃ karaṇaṃ śaktirucyate

plain_english: The divine will-power, existing by mere freedom — that same is Shiva's instrument; by her he knows and he acts.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryamātrasadbhāvā yā tvicchā śaktiraiśvarī śivasya saiva karaṇaṃ tayā vetti karoti ca

plain_english: The seven measurers from Shiva to sakala are twofold; by diminished or excessive power, their division differentiates the perceptible.
sanskrit_cite: ā śivātsakalāntaṃ ye mātāraḥ sapta te dvidhā nyagbhūtodriktaśaktitvāttadbhedo vedyabhedakaḥ

plain_english: Thus: perceptibility named is only the entity's own body — 'I know the perceptible through Caitra' — so what appears here?
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi vedyatā nāma bhāvasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ caitreṇa vedyaṃ vedmīti kiṃhyatra pratibhāsatām

plain_english: Surely here only Caitra-cognition shines; perceptibility so-called does not shine as the entity's property the way blue does.
sanskrit_cite: nanu caitrīyavijñānamātramatra prakāśate vedyatākhyastu no dharmo bhāti bhāvasya nīlavat

plain_english: And if perceptibility were the entity's property by nature, then everything would be perceptible to all, like pot, blue and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: vedyatā ca svabhāvena dharmo bhāvasya cettataḥ sarvānpratyeva vedyaḥ syāddhaṭanīlādidharmavat

plain_english: Now, though the entity bears perceptibility through perceiver-awareness force, that too is defective — like weaver-made cloth.
sanskrit_cite: atha vedakasaṃvittibalādvedyatvadharmabhāk bhāvastathāpi doṣo@sau kuvindakṛtavastravat

plain_english: But if that so-called perceptibility-property is itself unperceived, it is like a sky-flower; if it exists as perceived, there too is regress upon perceptibility.
sanskrit_cite: vedyatākhyastu yo dharmaḥ so@vedyaścetkhapuṣpavat vedyaścedasti tatrāpi vedyetatyanavasthitiḥ

plain_english: Then nothing would be perceptible, and the world would be stupefied — but, you say, let the body be declared as fashioned by the cognizer's conditioning.
sanskrit_cite: tato na kiṃcidvedyaṃ syānmūrchitaṃ tu jagadbhavet nanu vijñātrupādhyaṃ śo paskṛtaṃ vapurucyatām

plain_english: As this knowledge, whose nature is the entity's meaning-manifestation, is unreal — under single-knower knowability there is no knowability by another knower.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvasyārthaprakāśātma yathā jñānamidaṃ tvasat ekavijñātṛvedyatve na jñātrantaravedyatā

plain_english: Under all-knower knowability there is no single-knower knowability — therefore perceptibility so-called is no entity's property at all.
sanskrit_cite: samastajñātṛvedyatve naikavijñātṛvedyatā tasmānna vedyatā nāma bhāvadharmo@sti kaścana

plain_english: The entity's perceptibility is just that uprising of consciousness whose form is object-grasping, where awareness stands in itself.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvasya vedyatā saiva saṃvido yaḥ samudbhavaḥ arthagrahaṇarūpaṃ hi yatra vijñānamātmani

plain_english: The manifest object unites with it — counter to that stands this very perceptibility. Here we say: if perceptibility is no property of objects...
sanskrit_cite: samavaiti prakāśyo@rthastaṃ pratyeṣaiva vedyatā atra brūmaḥ padārthānāṃ na dharmo yadi vedyatā

plain_english: They would indeed be unknowable even when knowledge is truly described — as with the pot of broad-based form, even though it is real.
sanskrit_cite: avedyā eva te saṃsyurjñāne satyapi varṇite yathāhi pṛthubudhnādirūpe kumbhasya satyapi

plain_english: Cloth, not having that nature, does not take on broad-based form — so too, though knowledge exists conjoined with the knower.
sanskrit_cite: atadātmā paṭo naiti pṛthubudhnādirūpatām tathā satyapi vijñāne vijñātṛsamavāyini

plain_english: How would unperceptible-natured entities attain perceptibility? This is a very great absurdity — look at the entity itself.
sanskrit_cite: avedyadharmakā bhāvāḥ kathaṃ vedyatvamāpnuyuḥ anarthaḥ sumahāṃścaiṣa dṛśyatāṃ vastu yatsvayam

plain_english: Not light-natured is that consciousness — unlit, resting on that; unlit are mind, lamp, eye and the rest — and just so is that.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśātma na tatsaṃviccāprakāśā tadāśrayaḥ aprakāśo manodīpacakṣurādi tathaiva tat

plain_english: What is called being its light when the world sleeps on every side? Surely knowledge's object-illumination has lamp-form.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tatprakāśatāṃ nāma supte jagati sarvataḥ jñānasyārthaprakāśatvaṃ nanu rūpaṃ pradīpavat

plain_english: Nothing unprecedented is known here, and we perform no woman-dance — therefore let it be stated what form knowledge's object-illumination has.
sanskrit_cite: apūrvamatra viditaṃ narīnṛtyāmahe tataḥ arthaprakāśo jñānasya yadrūpaṃ tannirūpyatām

plain_english: If the object is light — is the object the form, or knowledge itself? Now, whatever illumination of the object there is, that is called its form.
sanskrit_cite: arthaḥ prakāśaścedrūpamartho vā jñānameva vā athārthasya prakāśo yastadrūpamiti bhaṇyate

plain_english: If the sixth is stated in the agent sense, the defect is hard to remove; now, this sixth in the object sense — the making-force stands firm at heart.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhī kartari cedukto doṣa eva duruddharaḥ atha karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyeṣā ṇyarthastatra hṛdi sthitaḥ

plain_english: And so we show this: what, does light shine? That thing is not without light either — and so nothing at all is.
sanskrit_cite: tathā cedaṃ darśayāmaḥ kiṃ prakāśaḥ prakāśate aprakāśo@pi naivāsau tathāpi ca na kiṃcana

plain_english: Then how is causal sense spoken of in the world when what abides is conscious? Its primary field is among the inert; toward consciousness it is only figurative.
sanskrit_cite: tarhi loke kathaṃ ṇyarthaḥ ucyate cetanasthitau mukhyo ṇyarthasya viṣayo jaḍeṣu tvaupacārikaḥ

plain_english: Thus though Caitra is able to go, taking the going as dependent on another, thinking so he speaks: I am gone, master.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi gantuṃ śakto@pi caitro@nyāyattatāṃ gateḥ manvāna eva vaktyasmi gamitaḥ svāmineti hi

plain_english: The master too, knowing the power in that going, seeing dependence plainly and fearing the stop, speaks: I shall make him go.
sanskrit_cite: svāmyapyasya gatau śaktiṃ buddhvā svādhīnatāṃ sphuṭam paśyannivṛttimāśaṃkya gamayāmīti bhāṣate

plain_english: Thus the causal connection is primary between the moved and the mover; another too, in the world, acts accordingly, from that intention.
sanskrit_cite: preryaprerakayorevaṃ maulikī ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ tadabhiprāyato@nyo@pi loke vyavaharettathā

plain_english: Here, in the words he makes the arrow go, one who posits the operation named impetus, thinking it the mover — that mover arises by figuration alone.
sanskrit_cite: śaraṃ gamayatītyatra punarvegākhyasaṃskriyām vidadhatprerakammanya upacāreṇa jāyate

plain_english: Here wind throws mountain, but both are inert and imagined by seers as mover and moved.
sanskrit_cite: vāyuradriṃ pātayatītyatra dvāvapi tau jaḍau draṣṭṛbhiḥ prerakapreryavapuṣā parikalpitau

plain_english: Thus in relation with an inert thing, primary causal sense is not; let it be elsewhere, for I have spread this out in detail.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ jaḍena saṃbandhe na mukhyā ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ āstāmanyatra vitatametadvistarato mayā

plain_english: Manifestation in meaning is metaphor; let it be; if it shines, then that itself is like a falling mountain.
sanskrit_cite: arthe prakāśanā seyamupacārastato bhavet astu cedbhāsate tarhi sa eva patadadrivat

plain_english: In metaphor, wind becomes by some cause; here 'throws mountain' has as cause an action done by that.
sanskrit_cite: upacāre nimittena kenāpi kila bhūyate vāyuḥ pātayatītyatra nimittaṃ tatkṛtā kriyā

plain_english: On the mountain, this attains fall from destruction of conjunction; but here knowledge of an object is not action at all.
sanskrit_cite: girau yenaiṣa saṃyoganāśādbhraṃśaṃ prapadyate iha tu jñānamarthasya na kiṃcitkarameva tat

plain_english: How can metaphor indeed be? That too is an unmanifest thing; an unmanifested object is not manifested by metaphor of manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: upacāraḥ kathaṃ nāma bhavetso@pi hyavastusan aprakāśita evārthaḥ prakāśatvopacārataḥ

plain_english: Just as a child is not burned by mere approach to fire, so approach alone lacks the seed of burning.
sanskrit_cite: tādṛgeva śiśuḥ kiṃ hi dahatyagnyupacārataḥ śiśau vahnyupacāre yadbījaṃ taikṣṇyādi tacca sat

plain_english: But where truth is established in consciousness, the approach of light has a fitting and clear seed.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśatvopacāre tu kiṃ bījaṃ yatra satyatā siddhe hi cetane yukta upacāraḥ sa hi sphuṭam

plain_english: That superimposition-natured thing lives by reconnection; yet no conscious knowledge exists as such.
sanskrit_cite: adhyāropātmakaḥ so@pi pratisaṃdhānajīvitaḥ na cādyāpi kimapyasti cetanaṃ jñānamapyadaḥ

plain_english: An unlit thing is lit by another; but how is a lamp the light of form?
sanskrit_cite: aprakāśaṃ tadanyena tatprakāśe@pyayaṃ vidhiḥ nanu pradīpo rūpasya prakāśaḥ kathamīdṛśam

plain_english: Here too these reasoning contrivances do not carry; a lamp lights form by its own form.
sanskrit_cite: atrāpi na vahantyetāḥ kiṃ nu yuktivikalpanāḥ yādṛśā svena rūpeṇa dīpo rūpaṃ prakāśayet

plain_english: Such knowledge shines by itself, but not so; this lamp gives beings abundant light.
sanskrit_cite: tādṛśā svayamapyeṣa bhāti jñānaṃ tu no tathā pradīpaścaiṣa bhāvānāṃ prakāśatvaṃ dadā[dhā]tyalam

plain_english: Otherwise they would not shine; therefore this previously stated light is supreme Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: anyathā na prakāśerannabhede cedṛśo vidhiḥ tasmātprakāśa evāyaṃ pūrvoktaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ

plain_english: As each thing-body shines clearly, so blueness, named, shines in some way.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā prakāśeta tattadbhāvavapuḥ sphuṭam evaṃ ca nīlatā nāma yathā kācitprakāśate

plain_english: Thus knowability shines; its fruit is the thing-part gone behind, and consciousness knows two.
sanskrit_cite: tadvaccakāsti vedyatvaṃ tacca bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam phalaṃ prakaṭatārthasya saṃvidveti dvayaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: Connection is protected from the opposite and mutual; thus a hidden thief is clearly knowable.
sanskrit_cite: vipakṣato rakṣitaṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ cāpi tanmithaḥ tathāhi nibhṛtaścauraścaitravedyamiti sphuṭam

plain_english: Having known, he did not take; though desire overcame him, she sees me respectfully with one third of an eye.
sanskrit_cite: buddhvā nādatta evāśu parīpsāvivaśo@pi san seyaṃ paśyati māṃ netratribhāgeneti sādaram

plain_english: The lover sees his own body sprinkled with nectar; it is not merely knowledge-awareness, but the thing-part gone behind.
sanskrit_cite: svaṃ dehamamṛteneva siktaṃ paśyati kāmukaḥ na caitajjñānasaṃvittimātraṃ bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam

plain_english: If knowability is a quality of all things, one must ask what that quality itself is.
sanskrit_cite: arthakriyākaraṃ taccenna dharmaḥ konvasau bhavet yaccoktaṃ vedyatādharmā bhāvaḥ sarvānapi prati

plain_english: The opponent's claim undermines itself, unlike the self-luminous Shiva view.
sanskrit_cite: syādityetatsvapakṣaghnaṃ duṣprayogāstravattava asmākaṃ tu svaprakāśaśivatāmātravādinām

plain_english: Nothing merely shines toward another; the blue pot is known to all.
sanskrit_cite: anyaṃ prati cakāstīti vaca eva na vidyate sarvānprati ca tannīlaṃ sa ghaṭaśceti yadvacaḥ

plain_english: Dull minds grasp a view that is almost unknown, while blueness is perceived in Rudra's body.
sanskrit_cite: tadapyaviditaprāyaṃ gṛhītaṃ mugdhabuddhibhiḥ nahi kālāgnirudrīyakāyāvagatanīlimā

plain_english: Your blue thing is not yellow; blue is not merely toward someone.
sanskrit_cite: tava nīlaḥ kiṃ nu pīto maivaṃ bhūnnatu nīlakaḥ na kaṃcitprati nīlo@sau nīlo vā yaṃ prati sthitaḥ

plain_english: Knowability would be gated by imagination, contrary to accepted knowledge as object-light.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ pratyeva sa vedyaḥ syātsaṃkalpadvārako@ntataḥ yathā cārthaprakāśātma jñānaṃ saṃgīryate tvayā

plain_english: The opponent cannot state the form of knower-dependent knowability.
sanskrit_cite: tathā tajjñātṛvedyatvaṃ bhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyatām na ca jñātātra niyataḥ kaścijjñāne yathā tava

plain_english: The knower of an object should be stated, and knowability shines toward all.
sanskrit_cite: arthe jñātā yadā yo yastadvedyaṃ vapurucyatām tattadvijñātṛvedyatvaṃ sarvānpratyeva bhāsatām

plain_english: The objector would become a deaf bull, since knowability does not shine toward another.
sanskrit_cite: ityevaṃ codayanmanye vrajedbadhiradhuryatām nahyanyaṃ prati vai kaṃcidbhāti sā vedyatā tathā

plain_english: When entity-form is stated, the opponent's rootless view is driven away by policy.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvasya rūpamityukte keyamasthānavaidhurī anena nītimārgeṇa nirmūlamapasāritā

plain_english: Knowability is not a regress like blue; it is the quality that makes all qualities.
sanskrit_cite: anavasthā tathā hyanyairnīlādyaiḥ sadṛśī na sā vedyatā kiṃtu dharmo@sau yadyogātsarvadharmavān

plain_english: The qualified thing attains knowability, as existence inheres in being.
sanskrit_cite: dharmī vedyatvamabhyeti sa sattāsamavāyavat brūṣe yathā hi kurute sattā satyasataḥ sataḥ

plain_english: Conjunction, though joined, reaches a final distinction whose form is difference, excluding what is not different.
sanskrit_cite: samavāyo@pi saṃśliṣṭaḥ śliṣṭānaśliṣṭatājuṣaḥ antyo viśeṣo vyāvṛttirūpo vyāvṛttivarjitān

plain_english: Whiteness moves between white and not-white, while the substrate itself stands endowed with blue and other qualities.
sanskrit_cite: vyāvṛttān śvetimā śuklamaśuklaṃ gamanaṃ tathā tadvannīlādidharmāṃśayukto dharmī svayaṃ sthitaḥ

plain_english: The unknowable gains knowability from knowable nature; knowability shines by itself, like blue and other qualities.
sanskrit_cite: avedyo vedyatārūpāddharmādvedyatvamāgataḥ vedyatā bhāsamānā ca svayaṃ nīlādidharmavat

plain_english: The unmanifest attains manifestness from self-manifest quality; indeed the universe takes rest in manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: aprakāśā svaprakāśāddharmādeti prakāśatām prakāśe khalu viśrāntiṃ viśvaṃ śrayati cettataḥ

plain_english: No other dependence is needed for the accomplished; as Shiva manifests difference by his own freedom.
sanskrit_cite: nānyā kācidapekṣāsya kṛtakṛtyasya sarvataḥ yathā ca śivanāthena svātantryādbhāsyate bhidā

plain_english: Thus knowability is called a quality like blue; knowability of being is established, so what aversion?
sanskrit_cite: nīlādivattathaivāyaṃ vedyatā dharma ucyate evaṃ siddhaṃ hi vedyatvaṃ bhāvadharmo@stu kā ghṛṇā

plain_english: But this must be considered: if knowability were uniform for all knowers, how could it be a fourteenth view?
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ tu cintyaṃ sakalaparyantoktapramātṛbhiḥ vedyatvamekarūpaṃ syāccāturdaśyamataḥ kutaḥ

plain_english: It is said that if the being-related form is complete, that all-pervading Bhairava, the lord himself, is declared.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate paripūrṇaṃ cedbhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyate tadvibhurbhairavo devo bhagavāneva bhaṇyate

plain_english: Now if an imagined gradual partial glory is tolerated, what then is accomplished by this stated imagination?
sanskrit_cite: atha tannijamāhātmyakalpitoṃ@śāṃśikākramaḥ sahyate kiṃ kṛtaṃ tarhi proktakalpanayānayā

plain_english: Therefore, when it shines by a body, as it shines, then it is that form; this is the supreme upanishad.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva yadā yena vapuṣā bhāti yadyathā tadā tathā tattadrūpamityeṣopaniṣatparā

plain_english: Caitra knows the knowable by two, by many, by mantra, and by that great lord Shiva with exalted power.
sanskrit_cite: caitreṇa vedyaṃ jānāmi dvābhyāṃ bahubhirapyatha mantreṇa tanmaheśena śivenodriktaśaktinā

plain_english: Being shines as another kind; thus variety of action and so on arises without enumeration.
sanskrit_cite: anyādṛśena vetyevaṃ bhāvo bhāti yathā tathā arthakriyādivaicitryamabhyetyaparisaṃkhyayā

plain_english: Thus the one-pointed whole assembly indeed considers dance and song as an ocean of nectar-essence.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hyekāgrasakalasāmājikajanaḥ khalu nṛttaṃ gītaṃ sudhāsārasāgaratvena manyate

plain_english: From that it is said, in the instruction of watching wrestler-actor, the identity of all knowers reveals the full form.
sanskrit_cite: tata evocyate mallanaṭaprekṣopadeśane sarvapramātṛtādātmyaṃ pūrṇarūpānubhāvakam

plain_english: If they are individually satisfied with cognition of that much meaning, what quality would their combined unity of knowers be?
sanskrit_cite: tāvanmātrārthasaṃvittituṣṭāḥ pratyekaśo yadi kaḥ saṃbhūya guṇasteṣāṃ pramātraikyaṃ bhavecca kim

plain_english: But when that thing is pregnant with a cluster of knowable properties and endowed with something other than dry prior form, then...
sanskrit_cite: yadā tu tattadvedyatvadharmasaṃdarbhagarbhitam tadvastu śuṣkātprāgrūpādanyadyuktamidaṃ tadā

plain_english: In scripture too, knowability of each produces distinct purposeful action, and thus in the Shri Malinivijayottara.
sanskrit_cite: śāstre@pi tattadvedyatvaṃ viśiṣṭārthakriyākaram bhūyasaiva tathāca śrīmālinīvijayottare

plain_english: Thus one should remember the sixfold path established by this; indeed the foundation by god is manifestation of which universe.
sanskrit_cite: tathā ṣaḍvidhamadhvānamanenādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret adhiṣṭhānaṃ hi devena yadviśvasya pravedanam

plain_english: Thus knowability, called a property of being, is established and shines.
sanskrit_cite: tadīśavedyatvenetthaṃ jñātaṃ prakṛtakāryakṛt evaṃ siddhaṃ vedyatākhyo dharmo bhāvasya bhāsate

plain_english: But in union with non-manifestation, own nature is said, clearly dispelling doubt of adjunct union.
sanskrit_cite: tadanābhāsayoge tu svarūpamiti bhaṇyate upādhiyogitāśaṅkāmapahastayato@sphuṭam

plain_english: By which form of one's own self the meaning shines, that own body; I know the pot here, endowed with knowability's coloring.
sanskrit_cite: svātmano yena vapuṣā bhātyarthastatsvakaṃ vapuḥ jānāmi ghaṭamityatra vedyatānuparāgavān

plain_english: The pot indeed shone by its own form, it is declared; but there, is self-knowable being dependent on mantra and so on?
sanskrit_cite: ghaṭa eva svarūpeṇa bhāta ityapadiśyate nanu tatra svayaṃvedyabhāvo mantrādyapekṣayā

plain_english: Also it indeed exists; let it be, but it does not appear; the unknowable indeed, of Meru having fire-body, supreme directions.
sanskrit_cite: api cāstyeva nanvastu natu sanpratibhāsate avedyameva kālāgnivapurmeroḥ parā diśaḥ

plain_english: "Mine" in consciousness: the supreme pure thing shines; though knowable due to shining, not that, as knowable, from shining.
sanskrit_cite: mameti saṃvidi paraṃ śuddhaṃ vastu prakāśate bhātatvādvedyamapi tanna vedyatvena bhāsanāt

plain_english: Indeed perception itself is imperceptible; in this way we inquire — this fifteen-aspected earth, and water and the like.
sanskrit_cite: avedyameva bhānaṃ hi tathā kamanuyuñjmahe evaṃ pañcadaśātmeyaṃ dharā tadvajjalādayaḥ

plain_english: From their unmanifest-end, perceptibility toward sakala is said — endowed from kalā down to earth.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktāntā yato@styeṣāṃ sakalaṃ prati vedyatā yattūcyate kalādyena dharāntena samanvitāḥ

plain_english: Sakala is so called by the excess of its six sheaths — the sheaths of arisen impure consciousness, attachment, kalā and the rest, of rasa.
sanskrit_cite: sakalā iti tatkośaṣaṭkodrekopalakṣaṇam udbhūtāśuddhacidrāgakalādirasakañcukāḥ

plain_english: The ones named sakala-abode have all sheaths subdued; the knowledge-akalās have that sheath destroyed — thus the conclusion.
sanskrit_cite: sakalālayasaṃjñāstu nyagbhūtākhilakañcukāḥ jñānākalāstu dhvastaitatkañcukā iti nirṇayaḥ

plain_english: Therefore even in pradhāna as object, the man with arisen sheath — the perceiver is indeed sakala, established according to the fifteen-aspect doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: tena pradhāne vedye@pi pumānudbhūtakañcukaḥ pramātāstyeva sakalaḥ pāñcadaśyamataḥ sthitam

plain_english: The fifteen-fold sakala, situated within earth to its end, even in sakala has an interior of sakala; even in the object of knowledge the knower is indeed.
sanskrit_cite: pāñcadaśyaṃ dharādhantarniviṣṭe sakale@pi ca sakalāntaramastyeva prameye@trāpi mātṛ hi

plain_english: The gross enveloped principles, yellow and so forth, number fourteen in earth and the other elements.
sanskrit_cite: sthūlāvṛtādisaṃkocatadanyavyāptṛtājuṣaḥ pītādyāḥ sthirakampratvāccaturdaśa dharādiṣu

plain_english: Inertness become own form, then knowerhood is declared as holding in the breath and body path in the Vijayottara.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpībhūtajaḍatāḥ prāṇadehapathe tataḥ pramātṛtājuṣaḥ proktā dhāraṇā vijayottare

plain_english: When measurability is assumed for man, the arisen sheath portion is measurable, but that is not his knowerhood.
sanskrit_cite: yadā tu meyatā puṃsaḥ kalāntasya prakalpyate tadudbhūtaḥ kañcukāṃśo meyo nāsya pramātṛtā

plain_english: Therefore knowerhood does not exist for the all-named one; thirteen-ness remains after excluding the power and powered duality.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ sakalasaṃjñasya pramātṛtvaṃ na vidyate trayodaśatvaṃ tacchaktiśaktimaddvayavarjanāt

plain_english: The subordinate sheath, mother, joined there with dissolution kala, and Maya-entered vijnanakala and others remain as before.
sanskrit_cite: nyagbhūtakañcuko mātā yukta[yata]statra layākalaḥ māyāniviṣṭo vijñānākalādyāḥ prāgvadeva tu

plain_english: In the Maya principle's knowable form, even the subordinate sheath is measurable, because Maya is very subtle and unified with the sheath.
sanskrit_cite: māyātattve jñeyarūpe kañcukanyagbhavo@pi yaḥ so@pi meyaḥ kañcukaikyaṃ yato māyā susūkṣmikā

plain_english: Indeed vijnanakala is here; then the mother sheath, even in Maya-entered kala, gives eleven-fold selfhood.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānākala evātra tato mātāpakañcukaḥ māyāniviṣṭe@pyakale tathetyekādaśātmatā

plain_english: In pure vijnana, the knowable well established after sheath destruction, motherhood belongs to mantras desiring awakening.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānakevale vedye kañcukadhvaṃsasusthite udbubhūṣuprabodhānāṃ mantrāṇāmeva mātṛtā

plain_english: Even those mantras, when measurable, have their lord as mother; but when full awareness arises there, measurability is removed.
sanskrit_cite: te@pi mantrā yadā meyāstadā mātā tadīśvaraḥ sa hyudbhavātpūrṇabodhastasminprāpte tu meyatām

plain_english: He of arisen full form is mother, the mantra great lord; when knowability is obtained there, supreme self-luminous Shiva appears.
sanskrit_cite: udbhūtapūrṇarūpo@sau mātā mantramaheśvaraḥ tasminvijñeyatāṃ prāpte svaprakāśaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ

plain_english: The knower is Shiva, whose self-sameness illuminates all knowable; he is not measurable because illumination does not depend on another.
sanskrit_cite: pramātā svakatādātmyabhāsitākhilavedyakaḥ śivaḥ pramātā no meyo hyanyādhīnaprakāśatā

plain_english: That measurability is not there, for he is the self-luminous lord; when no other is accepted in self-luminosity, measurability is absent.
sanskrit_cite: meyatā sā na tatrāsti svaprakāśo hyasau prabhuḥ svaprakāśe@tra kasmiṃścidanabhyupagate sati

plain_english: A regress from non-luminous to luminous is insurmountable; otherwise the universe would remain asleep.
sanskrit_cite: aprakāśātprakāśatve hyanavasthā duruttarā tataśca suptaṃ viśvaṃ syānna caivaṃ bhāsate hi tat

plain_english: Since Shiva is self-luminous, other logical displays are unnecessary.
sanskrit_cite: anyādhīnaprakāśaṃ hi tadbhātyanyastvasau śivaḥ ityasya svaprakāśatve kimanyairyuktiḍambaraiḥ

plain_english: The supreme soul was said from the beginning; yet knowability is questioned even in self-luminous Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: mānānāṃ hi paro jīvaḥ sa evetyuktamāditaḥ nanvasti svaprakāśe@pi śive vedyatvamīdṛśaḥ

plain_english: Otherwise instruction and teacherhood convention could not exist; truth is created thus by the supreme lord for knowability.
sanskrit_cite: upadeśo[śyo]padeṣṭṛtvavyavahāro@nyathā katham satyaṃ sa tu tathā sṛṣṭaḥ parameśena vedyatām

plain_english: Led to the mantra-lord level, he is made to meditate; thus knowable, he is not unlimited consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: nīto mantramaheśādikakṣyāṃ samadhiśāyyate tathābhūtaśca vedyo@sau nānavacchinnasaṃvidaḥ

plain_english: Knowability is fitting for the full one, but in reality shiva-selfhood is not found in knowable nature.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇasya vedyatā yuktā parasparavirodhataḥ tathā vedyasvabhāve@pi vastuto na śivātmatām

plain_english: Some state is relinquished so that meditation bears fruit; the glorious earlier scripture says it thus — Shiva is not divided in reality.
sanskrit_cite: ko@pi bhāvaḥ projjhatīti satyaṃ tadbhāvanā phalet śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ śivaḥ sākṣānna bhidyate

plain_english: By the direct word the whole meaning is made clear; yet endowed with oneness, Shiva would depend on that alone.
sanskrit_cite: sākṣātpadenāyamarthaḥ samastaḥ prasphuṭīkṛtaḥ nanvekarūpatāyuktaḥ śivastadvaśato bhavet

plain_english: What dispute is here in the great lord of the three-veda mantra — between the mantras of Maheśvara-īśa and the two kevalins?
sanskrit_cite: trivedatāmantramahānāthe kātra vivāditā maheśvareśamantrāṇāṃ tathā kevalinordvayoḥ

plain_english: Standing one by one from infinite differentiation, as with sakala indeed; then in the layakala, in the object, a perceiver exists — the layakala.
sanskrit_cite: anantabhedataikaikaṃ sthitā sakalavatkila tato layākale meye pramātāsti layākalaḥ

plain_english: Therefore thirteen-foldness may hold — not eleven-fold selfhood; even in the perceptibility of the vijñānākala another might be a jñānākala.
sanskrit_cite: atastrayodaśatvaṃ syāditthaṃ naikādaśātmatā vijñānākalavedyatve@pyanyo jñānākalo bhavet

plain_english: Mother, that eleven-foldness would not be, nor nine-selfhood; thus it is in the arising of the interval between the mantras and their lords.
sanskrit_cite: mātā tadekādaśatā syānnaiva tu navātmatā evaṃ mantratadīśānāṃ mantreśāntarasaṃbhave

plain_english: Although knowability yields nine, the seven and five are both asserted; the distinction is true and very clear.
sanskrit_cite: vedyatvānnava sapta syuḥ sapta pañca tu te katham ucyate satyamastyeṣā kalanā kiṃtu susphuṭaḥ

plain_english: As here in the whole there is difference, so it is not in the non-whole; the infinite interval and source difference make this clear.
sanskrit_cite: yathātra sakale bhedo na tathā tvakalādike anantāvāntaredṛkṣayonibhedavataḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: The fourteen-fold whole has difference; in dissolution, though only impression remains, difference is still true.
sanskrit_cite: caturdaśavidhasyāsya sakalasyāsti bheditā layākale tu saṃskāramātrātsatyapyasau bhidā

plain_english: The non-whole fits distinction for the whole; knowledge-only and similar states have no such difference.
sanskrit_cite: akalena viśeṣāya sakalasyaiva yujyate vijñānakevalādīnāṃ tāvatyapi na vai bhidā

plain_english: Shiva's free will alone unfolds difference for these; seeing distinction, one views the whole and others here.
sanskrit_cite: śivasvācchandyamātraṃ tu bhedāyaiṣāṃ vijṛmbhate ityāśayena saṃpaśyanviśeṣaṃ sakalādiha

plain_english: The Lord did not state thirteen and so on in dissolution; knowability may be a quality of being, but dissolution and non-whole remain.
sanskrit_cite: layākalādau novāca trāyodaśyādikaṃ vibhuḥ nanvastu vedyatā bhāvadharmaḥ kiṃtu layākalau

plain_english: They think not here indeed; there is no dependence on that. Let it be heard when consciousness-unity is established.
sanskrit_cite: manvāte neha vai kiṃcittadapekṣā tvasau katham śrūyatāṃ saṃvidaikātmyatattve@sminsaṃvyavasthite

plain_english: Consciousness is indeed even in the inert; but what question in what will be known? At the moment of self-knowledge, the dissolution-only one will be known.
sanskrit_cite: jaḍe@pi citirastyeva bhotsyamāne tu kā kathā svabodhāvasare tāvadbhotsyate layakevalī

plain_english: Awakening of this is two-fold, for mantra-hood and for becoming, arising from meditation power and other Vaishnava doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: dvividhaśca prabodho@sya mantratvāya bhavāya ca bhāvanādibalādanyavaiṣṇavādinayoditāt

plain_english: As impressed by varied superior support, the absorbed awakened one attains mantra-hood or lordship.
sanskrit_cite: yathāsvamādharauttaryavicitrātsaṃskṛtastathā līnaḥ prabuddho mantratvaṃ tadīśatvamathaiti vā

plain_english: Those devoid of freedom, subjected by delusion, awaken from dissolution, non-whole, and own impression for becoming.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryavarjitā ye tu balānmohavaśīkṛtāḥ layākalātsvasaṃskārātprabuddhyante bhavāya te

plain_english: The knowledge-particle awakens for mantra-lord or great-lord hood, or for mantra and so on, or even for worldly existence.
sanskrit_cite: jñānākalo@pi mantreśamaheśatvāya budhyate mantrāditvāya vā jātu jātu saṃsṛtaye@pi vā

plain_english: The descent differs in the state of the knower-yogi; it was said and taught by the world-lord desiring to create.
sanskrit_cite: avatāro hi vijñāniyogibhāve@sya bhidyate uktaṃ ca bodhayāmāsa sa sisṛkṣurjagatprabhuḥ

plain_english: In the prior scripture, eight pure knowers are mentioned; therefore the teachability of which two is considered.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānakevalānaṣṭāviti śrīpūrvaśāsane ataḥ prabhotsyamānatve yānayorbodhayogyatā

plain_english: By that power, fitness to be known arises here; for even in deep sleep, an unexpected arrival may come to the beloved.
sanskrit_cite: tadbalādvedyatāyogyabhāvenaivātra vedyatā tathāhi gāḍhanidre@pi priye@nāśaṅkitāgatām

plain_english: She will see me, not in her own limbs; thus Shiva too thinks of this knowability.
sanskrit_cite: māṃ drakṣyatīti nāṅgeṣu sveṣu mātyabhisārikā evaṃ śivo@pi manute etasyaitatpravedyatām

plain_english: When one will go and I create, then fitness alone is that knowability; the enjoyership of that being is so much.
sanskrit_cite: yāsyatīti sṛjāmīti tadānīṃ yogyataiva sā vedyatā tasya bhāvasya bhoktṛtā tāvatī ca sā

plain_english: The enjoyment of one in dissolution is wonderful; by whom is it imagined? As awareness itself is that enjoyment, manifest and manifest.
sanskrit_cite: layākalasya citro hi bhogaḥ kena vikalpyate yathā yathā hi samvittiḥ sa hi bhogaḥ sphuṭo@sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Even one capable of memory does not abandon the enjoyable state, though deeply asleep and bewildered, while the beloved's embraced body remains.
sanskrit_cite: smṛtiyogyo@pyanyathā vā bhogyabhāvaṃ na tūjjhati gāḍhanidrāvimūḍho@pi kāntāliṅgitavigrahaḥ

plain_english: He is called the enjoyer, and he thinks enjoyership, even lacking mere imagination, before some woman of a clan.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktaiva bhaṇyate so@pi manute bhoktṛtāṃ purā utprekṣāmātrahīno@pi kāṃcitkulavadhūṃ puraḥ

plain_english: Seeing a woman to be enjoyed, he rushes to delight; seeing her then, even one sharing the same intention does so.
sanskrit_cite: saṃbhokṣyamāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rabhasādyāti saṃmadam tāmeva dṛṣṭvā ca tadā samānāśayabhāgapi

plain_english: Otherwise another is not found in consciousness; what do we perceive here in the world? This established thing has vision as its intermediary cause.
sanskrit_cite: anyastathā na saṃvitte kamatropalabhāmahe loke rūḍhamidaṃ dṛṣṭirasminkāraṇamantarā

plain_english: One seems pleased as if immersed, another as if extinguished while debating; thus the difference of truth is extensively illustrated.
sanskrit_cite: prasīdatīva magneva nirvātīvetivādini itthaṃ vistaratastattvabhedo@yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ

plain_english: From mutual difference of power and possessor, and among those made, difference arises thus with other principles.
sanskrit_cite: śaktiśaktimatāṃ bhedādanyonyaṃ tatkṛteṣvapi bhedeṣvanyonyato bhedāttathā tattvāntaraiḥ saha

plain_english: For one counting differences and subdifferences there is no limit anywhere; therefore this varied world-arrangement is established.
sanskrit_cite: bhedopabhedagaṇanāṃ karvato nāvadhiḥ kvacit tata eva vicitro@yaṃ bhuvanādividhiḥ sthitaḥ

plain_english: Even in earthliness there is no equality between Rudra and Vishnu worlds; what talk of equality elsewhere, in enjoyment or in own form?
sanskrit_cite: pārthivatve@pi no sāmyaṃ rudravaiṣṇavalokayoḥ kā kathānyatra tu bhavedbhoge vāpi svarūpake

plain_english: That detail is not directly speakable, although it cannot be spoken; nevertheless, being told by path only, let it be distinguished.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca no vistaraḥ sākṣācchakyo yadyapi bhāṣitum tathāpi mārgamātreṇa kathyamāno vivicyatām

plain_english: When the seven mother-powers divide mutually, the form is forty-nine and more.
sanskrit_cite: saptānāṃ mātṛśaktīnāmanyonyaṃ bhedane sati rūpamekānnapañcāśatsvarūpaṃ cādhikaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: All is all-souled; therefore all powers of dissolution, art, and so on truly originate in the mother.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ sarvātmakaṃ yasmāttasmātsakalamātari layākalādiśaktīnāṃ saṃbhavo@styeva tattvataḥ

plain_english: Let that unclear portion be; the lord may give it, for among them and their mutual differences there is much difference.
sanskrit_cite: sa tvasphuṭo@stu bhedāṃśaṃ dātuṃ tāvatprabhurbhavet teṣāmapi ca bhedānāmanyonyaṃ bahubhedatā

plain_english: When principal differences are distinguished by water and similar elements, infinite rule variety is stated in the mode of principal difference.
sanskrit_cite: mukhyānāṃ bhedabhedānāṃ jalādyairbhedane sati mukhyabhedaprakāreṇa vidherānantyamucyate

plain_english: The arisen and subordinated powers of the whole clearly extend another difference.
sanskrit_cite: sakalasya samudbhūtāścakṣurādisvaśaktayaḥ nyagbhūtāśca pratanvanti bhedāntaramapi sphuṭam

plain_english: Thus another difference arises for dissolution powers and the like from impression, skill, or decay.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ layākalādīnāṃ tatsaṃskārapadoditāt pāṭavātprakṣayādvāpi bhedāntaramudīyate

plain_english: When one knows without entering the state of a subordinated power, another knowability indeed exists there.
sanskrit_cite: nyakkṛtāṃ śaktimāsthāyāpyudāsīnatayā sthitim anāviśyeva yadvetti tatrānyā vedyatā khalu

plain_english: For a knower, through entering, immersing, expanding, and revolving, another knowability difference suitable to action arises.
sanskrit_cite: āviśyeva nimajjyeva vikāsyeva vighūrṇya ca vidato vedyatānyaiva bhedo@trārthakriyocitaḥ

plain_english: When another power is concealed and some power clearly rises, another difference is to be known, like the view of a lute player.
sanskrit_cite: anyaśaktitirobhāve kasyāścitsusphuṭodaye bhedāntaramapi jñeyaṃ vīṇāvādakadṛṣṭivat

plain_english: Concealment and arising of power, from within another power and from being known or unknown, extend much difference.
sanskrit_cite: tirobhāvodbhavau śakteḥ svaśaktyantarato@nyataḥ cetyamānādacetyādvā tanvāte bahubhedatām

plain_english: Thus for earth and other principles, in whatever state exists, even that called pot, difference is shown there.
sanskrit_cite: evametaddharādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ yāvatī daśā kācidasti ghaṭākhyāpi tatra saṃdarśitā bhidaḥ

plain_english: Here also knowability is called identity with knowers; therefore the pot, all-knowable, is indeed whole.
sanskrit_cite: atrāpi vedyatā nāma tādātmyaṃ vedakaiḥ saha tataḥ sakalavedyo@sau ghaṭaḥ sakala eva hi

plain_english: As long as that is knowable by Shiva alone, Shiva indeed appears; for knowledge shines one-bodied to that extent.
sanskrit_cite: yāvacchivaikavedyo@sau śiva evāvabhāsate tāvadekaśarīro hi bodho bhātyeva yāvatā

plain_english: Now here the wholeness of all earth principle is shown, indeed as previously stated fifteen-fold.
sanskrit_cite: adhunātra samastasya dharātattvasya darśyate sāmastya evābhihitaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ puroditam

plain_english: The light that shines by non-difference of earth principle is indeed Shiva lord here; earth and Brahman is that opinion.
sanskrit_cite: dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate sa eva śivanātho@tra pṛthivī brahma tanmatam

plain_english: By Shiva's will, mantra great lords impel those striving to bestow powers dwelling in the earth principle.
sanskrit_cite: dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīrvitarītuṃ samudyatān prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ

plain_english: Impelled mantra lords, expressers of mantras, clearly practice yoga dwelling in the earth principle by Shiva knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: preryamāṇāstu mantreśā mantrāstadvācakāḥ sphuṭam dharātattvagataṃ yogamabhyasya śivavidyayā

plain_english: But bonded samkhya, vaishnava, and similar types, not reaching the eternal abode, enjoy the limited state of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: na tu pāśavasāṃkhyīyavaiṣṇavādidvitādṛśā aprāptadhruvadhāmāno vijñānākalatājuṣaḥ

plain_english: Those who, by enjoyment of principles, go to dissolution at kalpa end, endowed with deep sleep state, become pure dissolution beings.
sanskrit_cite: tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ sauṣuptāvasthayopetāste@tra pralayakevalāḥ

plain_english: In deep sleep, absorption into principle is clearly seen; otherwise, how would fixed dream vision arise?
sanskrit_cite: sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭameva hi lakṣyate anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃdṛṣṭirjāyate kutaḥ

plain_english: Deep sleep also appears variegated, with clear and unclear states, from seeing memory variety such as 'I slept happily'.
sanskrit_cite: sauṣuptamapi citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate asvāpsaṃ sukhamityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt

plain_english: When he awakens for a subtle moment from sleep, then memory is said to arise; memory is not born from object-born knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yadaiva sa kṣaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nidrāyaiva prabuddhyate tadaiva smṛtireṣeti nārthajajñānajā smṛtiḥ

plain_english: Therefore, what fools say—that memory of cotton and pleasant touch arises between awakenings—is untenable.
sanskrit_cite: tena mūḍhairyaducyeta prabuddhasyāntarāntarā tūlikādisukhasparśasmṛtireṣeti tatkutaḥ

plain_english: Here all persons to be known are earth-ascending, free from impurity mixed with great karma excitement.
sanskrit_cite: māhākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ

plain_english: The agitation in planning own activities of this sevenfold is that which is clearly said of the sevenfold powers.
sanskrit_cite: asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane prakṣobho yastadevoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ sphuṭam

plain_english: Shiva, indeed imperishable consciousness form, has three powers; those are conditioned by autonomy into grasper form.
sanskrit_cite: śivo hyacyutacidrūpastisrastacchaktayastu yāḥ tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītrākāratāvaśāt

plain_english: Mantra endings would stand threefold, indifferent like, due to object form coloring and grasper form condition.
sanskrit_cite: tridhā mantrāvasānāḥ syurudāsīnā iva sthitāḥ grāhyākāroparāgāttu grahītrākāratāvaśāt

plain_english: The three powers, will, knowledge, and action, are considered; sevenfold knowerhood arises thus from its agitation and measurehood.
sanskrit_cite: sakalāntāstu tāstisra icchājñānakriyā matāḥ saptadhetthaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ tatkṣobho mānatā tathā

plain_english: But that which is pure and inert, devoid of grasper, form, consciousness, and contact, is the universe's nature, threefold.
sanskrit_cite: yattu grahītṛtārūpasaṃvitsaṃsparśavarjitam śuddhaṃ jaḍaṃ tatsvarūpamitthaṃ viśvaṃ trikātmakam

plain_english: Thus even water and the rest would be said divided by differences; by this direction, mostly, it is found in all differences.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jalādyapi vadedbhedairbhinnaṃ mahāmatiḥ anayā tu diśā prāyaḥ sarvabhedeṣu vidyate

plain_english: This difference among mantra great lords is fifteenfold; nevertheless, because it lacks clarity, even though existing, it is not discussed.
sanskrit_cite: bhedo mantramaheśānteṣveṣa pañcadaśātmakaḥ tathāpi sphuṭatābhāvātsannapyeṣa na carcitaḥ

plain_english: And this is summarized by the creator in the previous Sri, which indeed says, by lordship with activity and so on, the waking state and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: etacca sūtritaṃ dhātrā śrīpūrve yadbravīti hi savyāpārādhipatvenetyādinā jāgradāditām

plain_english: Even in undivided Shiva, according to the subtle knowledge within, now in the prana-shakti-established net of principles, it is distinguished.
sanskrit_cite: abhinne@pi śive@ntaḥsthasūkṣmabodhānusārataḥ adhunā prāṇaśaktisthe tattvajāle vivicyate

plain_english: This difference, as fifteenfold and so on, Sri Shambhu taught; in all meaning here, in the ungraspable, there are sixteen moment-sparks.
sanskrit_cite: bhedo@yaṃ pāñcadaśyādiryathā śrīśaṃbhurādiśat samaste@rthe@tra nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ

plain_english: In the movement of thirty-six angulas, conceived as half and quarter angulas, the first there is supreme nondual, essence of undivided taste.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre sāṃśadvyaṅgulakalpitāḥ tatrādyaḥ paramādvaito nirvibhāgarasātmakaḥ

plain_english: The second is the form of grasper expansion, manifested; but the last has become self-nature by identity with graspedness.
sanskrit_cite: dvitīyo grāhakollāsarūpaḥ prativibhāvyate antyastu grāhyatādātmyātsvarūpībhāvamāgataḥ

plain_english: Indeed the penultimate grasper moment is not to be separately manifested; but from the third moment, six moments are established.
sanskrit_cite: pravibhāvyo na hi pṛthagupāntyo grāhakaḥ kṣaṇaḥ tṛtīyaṃ kṣaṇamārabhya kṣaṇaṣaṭkaṃ tu yatsthitam

plain_english: That nondiscursive state, consisting of rising discursive covering, that itself is known as Shiva's form, consisting of supreme power.
sanskrit_cite: tannirvikalpaṃ prodgacchadvikalpācchādanātmakam tadeva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ

plain_english: The second, middle, sixfold consists of supreme and lower levels; this discursive rise too has gone to gradual clarity.
sanskrit_cite: dvitīyaṃ madhyamaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parāparapadātmakam vikalparūḍhirapyeṣā kramātprasphuṭatāṃ gatā

plain_english: In the first hexad here, the three goddesses, touching opening and closing modes quickly, attain a sixfold state.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭke@tra prathame devyastisraḥ pronmeṣavṛttitām nimeṣavṛttitāṃ cāśu spṛśantyaḥ ṣaṭkatāṃ gatāḥ

plain_english: Thus in the second hexad too, what? Here, having reached the eclipse state by the object path, they stand as supreme and lower.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ dvitīyaṣaṭke@pi kiṃ tvatra grāhyavartmanā uparāgapadaṃ prāpya parāparatayā sthitāḥ

plain_english: In the first hexad here, those goddesses, from freedom's exuberance alone, even in desired conditioning, would remain not fallen from supreme form.
sanskrit_cite: ādye@tra ṣaṭke tā devyaḥ svātantryollāsamātrataḥ jighṛkṣite@pyupādhau syuḥ pararūpādavicyutāḥ

plain_english: There is also some excellence among them, increasing progressively, which is shown by wise possessors of discernment even after making it clear.
sanskrit_cite: asti cātiśayaḥ kaścittāsāmapyuttarottaram yo vivekadhanairdhīraiḥ sphuṭīkṛtyāpi darśyate

plain_english: Some, placing one pulse in the object and one also in the subject by identity, know a sevenfold and a sevenfold.
sanskrit_cite: kecittvekāṃ tuṭiṃ grāhye caikāmapi grahītari tādātmyena vinikṣipya saptakaṃ saptakaṃ viduḥ

plain_english: Striving for measuring in that subtle awareness, they experience what form there; what use are speech boasts?
sanskrit_cite: tadasyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vāgvikatthanaiḥ

plain_english: Thus the process from earth to root end, going by life breath, is taught by guru lineage order in difference, fifteenfold.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ dharādimūlāntaṃ prakriyā prāṇagāminī guruparvakramātproktā bhede pañcadaśātmake

plain_english: But by order, in lesser difference, deficiency would be even in pulses; in that, conceptualization decreases and clarity of the non-conceptual increases.
sanskrit_cite: kramāttu bhedanyūnatve nyūnatā syāttuṭiṣvapi tasyāṃ hrāso vikalpasya sphuṭatā cāvikalpinaḥ

plain_english: As indeed a long-suffering distressed person, afterward established in happiness, forgets that suffering by the path of happiness's rest.
sanskrit_cite: yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścādāttasukhasthitiḥ vismaratyeva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā

plain_english: So, even when conceptualization is gone, people rooted in experience do not regard that existence by the force of conceptualization's rest.
sanskrit_cite: tathā gatavikalpe@pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ vikalpaviśrāntibalāttāṃ sattāṃ nābhimanvate

plain_english: By decrease of conceptualization, conceptualization-barren supreme truth goes to manifestness of awareness nature; thus good intellect belongs to strivers in attention there.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvamitthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ

plain_english: In the connection of object and subject awareness, this attentiveness is that spoken there, all-desires-milking, because of that.
sanskrit_cite: grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā iyaṃ sā tatra tatroktā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ

plain_english: Thus, as duality decreases, the two tuṭis gradually and clearly go to deficiency.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ dvayaṃ dvayaṃ yāvannyūnībhavati bhedagam tāvattuṭidvayaṃ yāti nyūnatāṃ kramaśaḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: Therefore in Śiva-entry two tuṭis are praised; but that one tuṭi there is full, pure, and alone.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva śivāveśe dvituṭiḥ parigīyate ekā tu sā tuṭistatra pūrṇā śuddhaiva kevalam

plain_english: The second is Śiva-Śakti form, all-knowledge and action; absorbed in it, what does the yogi not know or do?
sanskrit_cite: dvitīyā śivaśaktirūpaiva sarvajñānakriyātmikā tasyāmavahito yogī kiṃ na vetti karoti vā

sanskrit_cite: tathā coktaṃ kallaṭena śrīmatā tuṭipātagaḥ lābhaḥ sarvajñakartṛtve tuṭeḥ pāto@parā tuṭiḥ

plain_english: In the first tuṭi all has gone to full unity everywhere; what there is knowable, doable, or named?
sanskrit_cite: ādyāyāṃ tu tuṭau sarvaṃ sarvataḥ pūrṇamekatām gataṃ kiṃ tatra vedyaṃ vā kāryaṃ vā vyapadeśabhāk

plain_english: Therefore the wise seek the initial Devī-pratibhā, blossoming with difference, for accomplishment of omniscience and so on.
sanskrit_cite: ato bhedasamullāsakalāṃ prāthamikīṃ budhāḥ cinvanti pratibhāṃ devīṃ sarvajñatvādisiddhaye

plain_english: That same Śakti of Śiva is said; in the third and later tuṭis, mantra-lords and their śaktis and so on arise in order.
sanskrit_cite: saiva śaktiḥ śivasyoktā tṛtīyādituṭiṣvatha mantrādidhināthatacchaktimantreśādyāḥ kramoditāḥ

plain_english: In them, fixing the mind with one-pointed attention, the respective siddhi-entrance arises by itself.
sanskrit_cite: tāsu saṃdadhataścittamavadhānaikadharmakam tattatsiddhisamāveśaḥ svayamevopajāyate

plain_english: Therefore, as multiplicity of difference is distance, so in consciousness many tuṭis are like non-contact with the desired object.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva yathā bhedabahutvaṃ dūratā tathā saṃvittau tuṭibāhulyādakṣārthāsaṃnikarṣavat

plain_english: As tuṭis decrease, difference decreases; so consciousness becomes nearer, up to Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā hi nyūnatvaṃ tuṭīnāṃ hrāsato bhidaḥ tathā tathātinaikaṭyaṃ saṃvidaḥ syācchivāvadhi

plain_english: The Śiva principle is said to be near from all sides; therefore no effort is found in entering it.

plain_english: As distance, so effort; thus meditation, action, and so on have no scope in Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā hi dūratvaṃ yatnayogastathā tathā bhāvanākaraṇādīnāṃ śive niravakāśatām

plain_english: Therefore indeed people think so, for let the world be seen as in perception of pot and so on.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva hi manyante saṃpradāyadhanā janāḥ tathā hi dṛśyatāṃ loko ghaṭādervedane yathā

plain_english: It appears as one with effort; so what is this internality in pleasure perception? They say consciousness-nearness.
sanskrit_cite: prayatnavānivābhāti tathā kiṃ sukhavedane āntaratvamidaṃ prāhuḥ saṃvinnaikaṭyaśālitām

plain_english: That consciousness-form manifestation and externality, its closing for beings, even near does not appear, so extreme distance.
sanskrit_cite: tāṃ ca cidrūpatonmeṣaṃ bāhyatvaṃ tannimeṣatām bhavināṃ tvantiko@pyevaṃ na bhātītyatidūratā

plain_english: Even far, having become near, appearance may be here; how then not like seed, sprout, vine, leaf, flower, fruit, and so on?
sanskrit_cite: dūre@pi hyantikībhūte bhānaṃ syāttvatra tatkatham na ca bījāṅkuralatādalapuṣpaphalādivat

plain_english: This sequential thing may be a consciousness thread there; indeed a sprout from seed, vine, and not a sprout from seed here from all.
sanskrit_cite: kramikeyaṃ bhavetsaṃvitsūtastatra kilāṅkuraḥ bījāllatā tvaṅkurānno bījādiha sarvataḥ

plain_english: The consciousness principle, shining and complete everywhere, is declared the cause of all, arisen everywhere, because.

plain_english: Therefore indeed, even in the pot, if this breath function shines, it may rest quickly; there indeed it may go to dissolution in the Shiva seed.

plain_english: But sequentiality is never a cause in Shiva selfhood; other mantra and lord and so on are not the cause, but that is of proximity.

plain_english: And from Shiva non-difference, what then in duality from nearness perception? By this direction all is always discriminated.

plain_english: Extended Bhairava indeed immediately has gone to consciousness-wheel lordship; thus the breath-goer difference is hidden by the Khechari wheel.

plain_english: By me, following Shambhava command, it is revealed: in this path, knowability having been attained, consciousness may arise.

plain_english: Of that, its own variety is called state-word: waking, dream, deep sleep, and the fourth, and beyond that.

plain_english: Thus they say five words in one Veda; there this pathway of principles runs from earth principle to Shiva.

plain_english: In that one knower, if necessarily, waking and the rest are shown; by Shambhunatha's grace this is known by me.

plain_english: What is to be superintended only here is never the superintender; the known object in experience is called waking.

plain_english: Things like Chaitra and Maitra are principles from earth; words become means of denotation; what? denotation too is cognition.
sanskrit_cite: caitramaitrādibhūtāni tattvāni ca dharāditaḥ abhidhākaraṇībhūtāḥ śabdāḥ kiṃ cābhidhā pramā

plain_english: The fourfold of knower, known, means of knowledge, and cognition; this universe is to be superintended; when waking, then it is remembered.
sanskrit_cite: pramātṛmeyatanmānapramārūpaṃ catuṣṭayam viśvametadadhiṣṭheyaṃ yadā jāgrattadā smṛtam

plain_english: For thus appears that blue within in cognition of thought-form; of the external, its superintender is the cognizer.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hi bhāsate yattannīlamantaḥ pravedane saṃkalparūpe bāhyasya tadadhiṣṭhātṛ bodhakam

plain_english: But that blue shines as external; for him no superintender-state exists in any way; that is called waking.
sanskrit_cite: yattu bāhyatayā nīlaṃ cakāstyasya na vidyate kathaṃcidapyadhiṣṭhātṛbhāvastajjāgraducyate

plain_english: There in appearing Chaitra, the body-part is called unawakened; the cognition-part is awakened and is the cognition-maker.
sanskrit_cite: tatra caitre bhāsamāne yo dehāṃśaḥ sa kathyate abuddho yastu mānāṃśaḥ sa buddho mitikārakaḥ

plain_english: Awakened, fully awakened, and cognition-only etc. form a sequence; fourfold indeed in bodily waking is proclaimed.
sanskrit_cite: prabuddhaḥ suprabuddhaśca pramāmātreti ca kramaḥ cāturvidhyaṃ hi piṇḍasthanāmni jāgrati kīrtitam

plain_english: Etc.; beyond-fourth however, because all-pervading, how separate? Also bodily waking-unawakened and awakened only are said.

plain_english: In the Shri Malini view, the presided-over element principle is called body-located.
sanskrit_cite: bhūtatattvābhidhānānāṃ yoṃ@śo@dhiṣṭheya ucyate piṇḍasthamiti taṃ prāhuriti śrīmālinīmate

plain_english: The worldly waking state is also called body-located, defined for yogis' accomplishment of yoga.

plain_english: The identity of a yogi seated in presided samadhi is body-located, measured and condensed.
sanskrit_cite: adhiṣṭheyasamāpattimadhyāsīnasya yoginaḥ tādātmyaṃ kila piṇḍasthaṃ mitaṃ piṇḍaṃ hi piṇḍitam

plain_english: For knowers established in discrimination, that is called all-around auspicious full by object existence.
sanskrit_cite: prasaṃkhyānaikarūḍhānāṃ jñānināṃ tu taducyate sarvatobhadramāpūrṇaṃ sarvato vedyasattayā

plain_english: Because the knower sees the universe full of all existence, its consciousness-nature shines.

plain_english: Because of the triple form of world, yoga, and discrimination, three names are spoken; the same rule applies in dreams.

plain_english: The knowable remains, previously described as real and element-principle-named, when superimposed on the presiding instrument state.

plain_english: That dream is primarily to be known, since it appears similar to a knowable on an imaginary path.

sanskrit_cite: lokarūḍho@pyasau svapnaḥ sāmyaṃ cābāhyarūpatā utprekṣāsvapnasaṃkalpasmṛtyunmādādidṛṣṭiṣu

plain_english: The clear knowable is waking-primary; what is unclear there appears with a clear presider.
sanskrit_cite: vispaṣṭaṃ yadvedyajātaṃ jāgranmukhyatayaiva tat yattu tatrāpyavispaṣṭaṃ spaṣṭādhiṣṭhātṛ bhāsate

plain_english: A knowable gone to another imagination is called a dream state; then it knows its own lack of externality.

plain_english: There also, in that unsteady selfhood, one should imagine the fourfoldness as before.
sanskrit_cite: pramātrantarasādhārabhāvahānyasthirātmate tatrāpi cāturvidhyaṃ tat prāgdiśaiva prakalpayet

plain_english: Coming and going, well-scattered, gathered, well-composed; here too the worldly name dream is thus this.
sanskrit_cite: gatāgataṃ suvikṣiptaṃ saṃgataṃ susamāhitam atrāpi pūrvavannāma laukikaṃ svapna ityadaḥ

plain_english: Sleep is considered non-grasping of desired external states; it is a state of all paths, with life-breath and thought of going.
sanskrit_cite: bāhyābhimatabhāvānāṃ svāpo hyagrahaṇaṃ matam sarvādhvanaḥ padaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃkalpo@vagamātmakaḥ

plain_english: Yogis know absorption in that state and the existence of the knowable, without considering the external, everywhere.

sanskrit_cite: vedye svātantryabhāg jñānaṃ svapnaṃ vyāptitayā bhajet mānabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā svapno hyāmarśanātmakaḥ

plain_english: The reflection of the knowable is indeed called the support of the measurable, from the support-base of the previously said permanent body.
sanskrit_cite: vedyacchāyo@vabhāso hi meye@dhiṣṭhānamucyate yattvadhiṣṭhātṛbhūtādeḥ pūrvoktasya vapurdhruvam

plain_english: The seed of the universe, that silent, is called deep sleep; in experience and imagination, that seer is indeed he.
sanskrit_cite: bījaṃ viśvasya tattūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ sauṣuptamucyate anubhūtau vikalpe ca yo@sau draṣṭā sa eva hi

plain_english: Deep sleep is called sleep because it resembles ordinary sleep, though being is not grasped there.
sanskrit_cite: na bhāvagrahaṇaṃ tena suṣṭhu suptatvamucyate tatsāmyāllaukikīṃ nidrāṃ suṣuptaṃ manvate budhāḥ

plain_english: The primary mother state, with seed-being and silent nature, is declared deep sleep.
sanskrit_cite: bījabhāvo@thāgrahaṇaṃ sāmyaṃ tūṣṇīṃsvabhāvatā mukhyā mātṛdaśā seyaṃ suṣuptākhyā nigadyate

plain_english: Yogis know indifference through absorption while abiding in form.
sanskrit_cite: rūpakatvācca rūpaṃ tattādātmyaṃ yoginaḥ punaḥ rūpasthaṃ tatsamāpattyaudāsīnyaṃ rūpiṇāṃ viduḥ

plain_english: Great pervasion follows because a contraction of the knowable is absent.
sanskrit_cite: prasaṃkhyānavataḥ kāpi vedyasaṃkocanātra yat nāsti tena mahāvyāptiriyaṃ tadanusārataḥ

plain_english: Even for the indifferent one, the knowable is fourfold through superimposition on elements.
sanskrit_cite: udāsīnasya tasyāpi vedyaṃ yena caturvidham bhūtādi tadupādhyutthamatra bhedacatuṣṭayam

plain_english: A vast, peaceful, clear cognition-natured form stands upon the knower.
sanskrit_cite: uditaṃ vipulaṃ śāntaṃ suprasannamathāparam yattu pramātmakaṃ rūpaṃ pramāturupari sthitam

plain_english: The fourth state is the absorption of power, reached by falling away from fullness, aim, and indifference.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇatāgamanaunmukhyamaudāsīnyātparicyutiḥ tatturyamucyate śaktisamāveśo hyasau mataḥ

plain_english: Some call consciousness self-luminous; it is distinct from object, means, and knower, because the triad exists for that purpose.
sanskrit_cite: sā saṃvitsvaprakāśā tu kaiściduktā prameyataḥ mānānmātuśca bhinnaiva tadarthaṃ tritayaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: Object, means, and knower form the triad; he too rests clearly in that measurement, and that goddess is the life of the whole world.
sanskrit_cite: meyaṃ māne mātari tat so@pi tasyāṃ mitau sphuṭam viśrāmyatīti saivaiṣā devī viśvaikajīvitam

plain_english: Transcending form, seeing, and I, one abides; relying on door-only means and seeing without means.
sanskrit_cite: rūpaṃ dṛśāhamityaṃśatrayamuttīrya vartate dvāramātrāśritopāyā paśyāmītyanupāyikā

plain_english: Knowerhood, whose nature is freedom, shines as the fourth form of consciousness; itself light, that is it.
sanskrit_cite: pramātṛtā svatantratvarūpā seyaṃ prakāśate saṃvitturīyarūpaivaṃ prakāśātmā svayaṃ ca sā

plain_english: In absorption identity knowerhood becomes clear; from absorption coloring meanshood arises, and objecthood again.
sanskrit_cite: tatsamāveśatādātmye mātṛtvaṃ bhavati sphuṭam tatsamāveśoparāgānmānatvaṃ meyatā punaḥ

plain_english: From absorption proximity, that grace, and dissolution of object difference, that diseaseless state is said.
sanskrit_cite: tatsamāveśanaikaṭyāttrayaṃ tattadanugrahāt vedyādibhedagalanāduktā seyamanāmayā

plain_english: From means-grace establishment activity is said; waking and other states are established as power of god.
sanskrit_cite: mātrādyanugrahādādhānātsavyāpāreti bhaṇyate jāgradādyapi devasya śaktitvena vyavasthitam

plain_english: Other and higher-lower are twofold; that is higher, but this, fallen from formality and indifference, turns toward fullness.
sanskrit_cite: aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca dvidhā tatsā parā tviyam rūpakatvādudāsīnāccyuteyaṃ pūrṇatonmukhī

plain_english: In that state there is absorption; the yogi, through fullness-aim yoga, sees the universe beyond form and becomes full of that.
sanskrit_cite: daśā tasyāṃ samāpattī rūpātītaṃ tu yoginaḥ pūrṇataunmukhyayogitvādviśvaṃ paśyati tanmayaḥ

plain_english: Well-counted accumulation is held; in this, no other fourth state is possible indeed.
sanskrit_cite: prasaṃkhyātā pracayatasteneyaṃ pracayo matā naitasyāmaparā turyadaśā saṃbhāvyate kila

plain_english: Consciousness indeed shines as object by knowing only; waking and other prior states are possible for her, because.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvinna kila vedyā sā vittvenaiva hi bhāsate jāgradādyāstu saṃbhāvyāstisro@syāḥ prāgdaśā yataḥ

plain_english: By threefold grace this is said in trika teaching: manonmana is infinite and all-purpose by distinction.
sanskrit_cite: tritayānugrahātseyaṃ tenoktā trikaśāsane manonmanamanantaṃ ca sarvārthamiti bhedataḥ

plain_english: But that full unlimited bliss-laden beyond-fourth they call that same supreme state.
sanskrit_cite: yattu pūrṇānavacchinnavapurānandanirbharam turyātītaṃ tu tatprāhustadeva paramaṃ padam

plain_english: Here yoga has no real existence because meditation is absent; in the independent immeasurable state, meditatability is nowhere.
sanskrit_cite: nātra yogasya sadbhāvo bhāvanāderabhāvataḥ aprameye@paricchinne svatantre bhāvyatā kutaḥ

plain_english: Because yoga and the rest are absent, no name is given to the lord in this; by power of distinction this form is by fullness union.
sanskrit_cite: yogādyabhāvatastena nāmāsminnādiśadvibhuḥ prasaṃkhyānabalāttvetadrūpaṃ pūrṇatvayogataḥ

plain_english: Here anuttara is said, called great accumulation; from fullness only, possibility of differences in this is not indeed.
sanskrit_cite: anuttarādiha proktaṃ mahāpracayasaṃjñitam pūrṇatvādeva bhedānāmasyāṃ saṃbhāvanā na hi

plain_english: For refuting that, difference is not said as qualifier in this; ever-risen thus indicates all-pervasion.
sanskrit_cite: tannirāsāya naitasyāṃ bheda ukto viśeṣaṇam satatoditamityetatsarvavyāpitvasūcakam

plain_english: Indeed difference never becomes one anywhere; in beyond-fourth, difference one ever-risen thus this.
sanskrit_cite: na hyeka eva bhavati bhedaḥ kvacana kaścana turyātīte bheda ekaḥ satatodita ityayam

plain_english: Therefore foolish doctrine; nondifference of this is established, but in holy previous scripture by him said, knowers understand other state-standing.
sanskrit_cite: mūḍhavādastena siddhamavibheditvamasya tu śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ padasthamaparaṃ viduḥ

plain_english: Mantras and their lords with remainder are praised as form-standing; beyond form supreme power acts without disease.
sanskrit_cite: mantrāstatpatayaḥ seśā rūpasthamiti kīrtyate rūpātītaṃ parā śaktiḥ savyāpārāpyanāmayā

plain_english: Pure shiva beyond all, established in own self, is to be known; having known him one is liberated.
sanskrit_cite: niṣprapañco nirābhāsaḥ śuddhaḥ svātmanyavasthitaḥ sarvātītaḥ śivo jñeyo yaṃ viditvā vimucyate

plain_english: Thus holy shambhunatha represented real existence in waking and so on.
sanskrit_cite: iti śrīsumatiprajñācandrikāśāntatāmasaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthaḥ sadbhāvaṃ jāgradādau nyarūpayat

plain_english: But others speak another mode resorted; the form of waking and so on is now examined.
sanskrit_cite: anye tu kathayantyeṣāṃ bhaṅgīmanyādṛśīṃ śritāḥ yadrūpaṃ jāgradādīnāṃ tadidānīṃ nirūpyate

plain_english: Waking perception arises through sense activity and repeatedly grasps external forms.
sanskrit_cite: tatrākṣavṛttimāśritya bāhyākāragraho hi yaḥ tajjāgratsphuṭamāsīnamanubandhi punaḥ punaḥ

plain_english: Dream is self-created imagination, opposite to waking, conditioned by impurity and action.
sanskrit_cite: ātmasaṃkalpanirmāṇaṃ svapno jāgradviparyayaḥ layākalasya bhogo@sau malakarmavaśānnatu

plain_english: Deep sleep becomes stable through night absence and limited enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: sthirībhavenniśābhāvātsuptaṃ saukhyādyavedane jñānākalasya malataḥ kevalādbhogamātrataḥ

plain_english: Three powers remain situated in the fourth state.
sanskrit_cite: bhedavantaḥ svato@bhinnāścikīrṣyante jaḍājaḍāḥ turye tatra sthitā mantratannāthādhīśvarāstrayaḥ

plain_english: Beings become self-nondual as they enter bhairava knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yāvadbhairavabodhāntaḥpraveśanasahiṣṇavaḥ bhāvā vigaladātmīyasārāḥ svayamabhedinaḥ

plain_english: In the beyond-fourth state, clear form is considered waking.
sanskrit_cite: turyātītapade saṃsyuriti pañcadaśātmake yasya yadyatsphuṭaṃ rūpaṃ tajjāgraditi manyatām

plain_english: Unstable appearances are dream, unclear ones are sleep.
sanskrit_cite: yadevāsthiramābhāti sapūrvaṃ svapna īdṛśaḥ asphuṭaṃ tu yadābhāti suptaṃ tattatpuro@pi yat

plain_english: The fourth state is a thread-like continuity grasped in all differences.
sanskrit_cite: trayasyāsyānusaṃdhistu yadvaśādupajāyate sraksūtrakalpaṃ tatturyaṃ sarvabhedeṣu gṛhyatām

plain_english: Beyond the fourth state is nondual joy that melts all difference.
sanskrit_cite: yattvadvaitabharollāsadrāvitāśeṣabhedakam turyātītaṃ tu tatprāhuritthaṃ sarvatra yojayet

plain_english: The wise follow all states in order everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: layākale tu svaṃ rūpaṃ jāgrattatpūrvavṛtti tu svapnādīti kramaṃ sarvaṃ sarvatrānusaredbudhaḥ

plain_english: In the full lord, consciousness beyond the fourth is named.
sanskrit_cite: ekatrāpi prabhau pūrṇe citturyātītamucyate ānandasturyamicchaiva bījabhūmiḥ suṣuptatā

plain_english: Knowledge power is dream and action power is waking in reality.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaśaktiḥ svapna uktaḥ kriyāśaktistu jāgṛtiḥ na caivamupacāraḥ syātsarvaṃ tatraiva vastutaḥ

plain_english: The great lord clearly stated this primacy in the earlier treatise.
sanskrit_cite: na cenna kvāpi mukhyatvaṃ nopacāro@pi tatkvacit etacchrīpūrvaśāstre ca sphuṭamuktaṃ maheśinā

plain_english: The waking state consists of own form, power, and whole in fifteenfold difference.
sanskrit_cite: tatra svarūpaṃ śaktiśca sakalaśceti tattrayam iti jāgradavastheyaṃ bhede pañcadaśātmake

plain_english: Beyond the fourth, power and Shambhu belong to dream and deep sleep in thirteenfold form.
sanskrit_cite: akalau svapnasauṣupte turyaṃ mantrādivargabhāk turyātītaṃ śaktiśaṃbhū trayodaśābhidhe punaḥ

plain_english: Own form appears apart from waking as before, with two in waking-dream-sleep and fourth as before.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpaṃ jāgradanyattu prāgvatpralayakevale svaṃ jāgratsvapnasupte dve turyādyatra ca pūrvavat

plain_english: Five waking states arise, including mantras, leaders, lords, power, and Shambhu.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānākalabhede@pi svaṃ mantrā mantranāyakāḥ tadīśāḥ śaktiśaṃbhvitthaṃ pañca syurjāgradādayaḥ

plain_english: In sevenfold mantra distinction, five states are named as waking and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: saptabhede tu mantrākhye svaṃ mantreśā maheśvarāḥ śaktiḥ śaṃbhuśca pañcoktā avasthā jāgradādayaḥ

plain_english: The essential nature is the five powers in the mantra-lord, in fivefold division.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpaṃ mantramāheśī śaktirmantramaheśvaraḥ śaktiḥ śaṃbhurimāḥ pañca mantreśe pañcabhedake

plain_english: Own action, knowledge, will, Shambhu, and the fifth are established in the threefold division of the great lord, including waking and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: svaṃ kriyā jñānamicchā ca śaṃbhuratra ca pañcamī maheśabhede trividhe jāgradādi nirūpitam

plain_english: Through activity, lordship, abundance, impelling, cessation of will, and abiding in his own state, Shiva, though one, is fivefold.
sanskrit_cite: vyāpārādādhipatyācca taddhānyā prerakatvataḥ icchānivṛtteḥ svasthatvācchiva eko@pi pañcadhā

plain_english: Thus this tattva path has been shown by us in detail, and then...
sanskrit_cite: ityeṣa darśito@smābhistattvādhvā vistarādatha
